names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 7 Αυγούστου, «Όσιος Ωρ», with the rank words and the epithets left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue’s second heading for the Julian 7 August, „Преп. Ор. Отшелник Тиваидски.“ — Преп. left off, which §5 maps to `venerable`, and Отшелник left off, which it maps to `hermit` and which is written into `types` by this reading. **Тиваидски is kept**: it is a toponym and not a rank, and it is the only thing left in the heading that distinguishes him. Without it the form would be a bare «Ор» of two letters, which is below the length at which the gate folds a form at all and which `usableName` would refuse; `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` measured both and reports that the two-word form adds a key no other folder holds while the bare one adds no key at all. The heading’s Thebaid disagrees with the Nitria of this folder’s display name, which came from saint.gr; the disagreement is recorded in the row note and the display name is not touched.

Name page 1675 of days.pravoslavie.ru is «Ор Фиваидский, пустынник»; «пустынник», hermit, is a rank word and is stripped. The day line gives the genitive «Ора Фиваидского». `fk.mjs` on the stored string returns NONE.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 7 августа ст. ст. — «Прп. Ора Фиваидского (ок. 390).»

attestations.note: The day's sixth entry and the same menologion day as the folder's Greek and Serbian rows; the «(ок. 390)» is the about-390 the folder already holds. THE EPITHET DISAGREES WITH THE SLUG AND IS NOT CHANGED: this calendar calls him Фиваидский, of the Thebaid, and the Serbian form the folder already stores agrees with it — «Ор Тиваидски» — while the slug and the display name say Nitria, which came off saint.gr. One man, two deserts named for him by different calendars; the display name is left alone and the disagreement recorded, a renaming being an author's and not a reader's. The day page prints no hymn under his name. THE EPITHET, READ AGAIN ON 13 OCTOBER 2026 AGAINST BOTH SOURCES, AND THE SLUG STILL NOT TOUCHED. The question put was whether the books disagree about the desert or whether saint.gr is simply wrong about it. They disagree, and the weight is not even. **This calendar names the Thebaid three times.** The day's line declines it, «Прп. Ора Фиваидского (ок. 390).»; name page 1675 heads it, «Ор Фиваидский, пустынник»; and the life page life4393 — which the earlier reading of this row did not open, and which is the fullest account of the three books — puts it in the narrative and not in a by-name: «Преподобный Ор (IV) в молодых годах удалился в Фиваидскую пустыню и подвизался в совершенном уединении много лет, ведя суровую отшельническую жизнь.» The Охридски пролог agrees from the other side with „Отшелник Тиваидски“. **saint.gr names Nitria once, in a clause, and gives him no by-name at all.** Its heading is the bare «Όσιος Ωρ» and its whole entry opens «Ο Όσιος αυτός ασκήτευε στο όρος της Νιτρίας»; page 766 was fetched again and read whole, and that sentence is the only place in any of the three books where Nitria appears. So the corpus's display name and slug rest on the minority reading, out of the thinnest of the three entries, and the majority reading is a by-name two calendars attach to him and one of them also narrates. That is said here rather than acted on: **a slug rename is an operation with aliases and is not a reader's to improvise**, and the folder keeps all three readings instead — Νιτρίας in the display name and the life's first paragraph, Фиваидский in the stored `ru` form, Тиваидски in the stored `sr` form, and the disagreement named in three notes and in the life. WHAT life4393 CORROBORATES AND WHAT IT ADDS. It corroborates the age and the year this folder already holds — «Скончался он 90 лет около 390 года», the ninety of saint.gr and the about-390 of the Prologue, arrived at independently — and `dates` is therefore NOT TOUCHED, the note there standing as the Prologue's. It adds the fourth century in the line's own «(IV)», the angel who told him the Lord was entrusting the salvation of many to him, the gift of reading Scripture given to a man untaught his letters from childhood, his never going in to table without having communicated that day, his teaching the brethren about a solitary's temptations as though he knew them only from other hermits, the disciples' thoughts open to him, and up to a thousand monks in the houses he founded. All of that is written into the life. It names nobody, so there is no `related` row and no new type: «пустынник» is the `hermit` the Serbian heading already gave. The day page's hymns were read again and it carries none under his name.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Αυγούστου — «Όσιος Ωρ»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Αυγούστου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The whole of the entry is one paragraph and it gives no year, so there is no `dates` object; it does give his age at repose, ninety. He is not the corpus's `or-the-martyr-22-august`, a martyr whom the Romanian calendar keeps on 22 August; this is the ascetic of the mountain of Nitria who founded monasteries and reposed in peace. No `locations` object is proposed from the name of a mountain. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page, which was grepped for there and not on the listing. The page prints no apolytikion and no kontakion, so this folder takes no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 20.08.2026 (7. август ст. ст.) — „Преп. Ор. Отшелник Тиваидски.“

attestations.note: The day’s second of five entries. His row was `undocumented` and the Greek line was this folder’s only book. **A RANK WORD IN THE HEADING THAT THE FOLDER DID NOT HAVE, AND IT IS WRITTEN.** „Преп. Ор. Отшелник Тиваидски.“ — Отшелник, a hermit, which §5 maps to `hermit`. The folder held `venerable` and `abbot` with `office` «Abbot», both from the Greek; `hermit` is added. **This is the one type this block has been able to add from a heading**, and it is the mirror of the Julian 5 August, where `deaconess` was in a body and had to be refused. It also agrees with what the folder already says: saint.gr has him live as a hermit for a few years before the brotherhoods, and „Када себе добро утврди и просвети у самоћи, тада основа постепено неколико манастира, и би изврстан духовни вођ и наставник многих монаха.“ has him found the monasteries only after he had established and enlightened himself in solitude. **A YEAR ON A FOLDER THAT HELD NO DATE AT ALL.** „Упокоји се у дубокој старости око 390 год.“ — he reposed in deep old age, about 390 — is written as `death` 390–390, display «about 390», basis traditional, which is the shape 118 folders of this corpus already use for an око year. **No `birth`**: „Руфин који га посети овако га описује: „У својој одећи он је личио на ангела Божјег, деведесетолетни старац с дугом брадом као снег белом, веома пријатне спољашности. Поглед његов светлио се нечим надчовечанским.““ calls him a ninety-year-old elder, and 390 less 90 is arithmetic and not a reading — the ninety is also the age saint.gr gives at his death, which is a different claim from an age at a visit, and the entry does not say the visit was at the end. **THE PLACE IN THE HEADING DISAGREES WITH THE ONE IN THE DISPLAY NAME, AND NOTHING IS RENAMED.** This book calls him Тиваидски, of the Thebaid; saint.gr put his asceticism on the mountain of Nitria and this corpus took «Or of Nitria» from that. Both are in Egypt and several hundred miles apart. The display name is the corpus’s own choice and is not this book’s to move; the Thebaid is kept in the stored `sr` form, where it is what the heading prints, and the disagreement is recorded here. **NO `related` ROW.** „Руфин који га посети овако га описује: „У својој одећи он је личио на ангела Божјег, деведесетолетни старац с дугом брадом као снег белом, веома пријатне спољашности. Поглед његов светлио се нечим надчовечанским.““ is a description of him by Руфин, who visited him — and **a visit is a meeting and would be a relation if he had a folder**. He has none: `ls saints | grep -iE "^rufin"` returns `rufinus-7-may`, `rufinus-of-rome` and `rufinus-the-deacon`, a martyr, a martyr and a deacon, none of them the writer who went round the monks of Egypt. Ruling 3 names him here and writes nothing, and his name is safe in the life because a one-word display name is not in the cross-linker’s index. The disciple of „Једном га опомену ученик, да је дошао Васкрс, и да треба празновати. Чувши то он изађе напоље, диже руке к небу, и три дана проведе у молитви без одмора. Па објасни ученику: „То и јесте празновање Васкрса за монаха, да ум свој узвиси и с Богом сједини“.“ is unnamed. No `locations`: the Thebaid is a region in a heading and not a point. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion: the day carries the verse only, which is Bishop Nikolai’s own and belongs to no person.

death.note: The folder held no date: saint.gr gives it no year at all, only an age. The Охридски пролог for 7. август ст. ст.: „Упокоји се у дубокој старости око 390 год.“ — he reposed in deep old age, about 390. No `birth` is written: the entry calls him a ninety-year-old elder inside Rufinus’s description of a visit, which is not an age at death, and 390 less 90 would be arithmetic rather than a reading (6 October 2026).
